clue.text: Difficulty in breathing whilst sleeping during the winter

indicators.note: a difficulty is trouble or a snag, so the following letters get into a tangle and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices their breathing becomes laboured while dozing through the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficulty in breathing' reads as a medical phrase, but 'Difficulty' is the anagram signal and both IN and BREATHING are the fodder, eleven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as bears and hedgehogs spend the cold season in a dormant state, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Impetuous chap who sits in the sun without a hat!

definitions.text: who sits in the sun without a hat!

explanation.surface: A rash fellow is sketched as someone who sunbathes bareheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: a bareheaded sunbather ends up with a scalp that is literally warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered man is commonly called this; the literal sense is a scalp heated by strong sunshine.

clue.text: Cultivate second class grass

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second class
a reed is a tall grass growing by water

explanation.surface: A gardener grows a lesser variety of lawn grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise plants or animals selectively is a synonym of rearing or cultivating them.

clue.text: River rose alarmingly and created a lake

indicators.note: something done alarmingly is wild and disturbing, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river in flood rises frighteningly and forms a body of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like a verb of rising water; with 'River' it is the anagram fodder, signalled by 'alarmingly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial lake built to store a water supply carries this name.

clue.text: Light tune at end of day

parts.note: an air is a melody

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here the last of day

explanation.surface: A gentle melody plays as evening falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Something light and breezy, open to the breeze, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: It's not right to dine in a mess on US money

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
something in a mess is jumbled up, so the letters of dine get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a cent is a US coin, a hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: Eating sloppily while being paid in dollars is frowned upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' sounds like a military dining hall, but it is the anagram signal, and 'on' places the scrambled piece above the coin in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper or offensive behaviour is morally wrong, which is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Start up on street and go about with enthusiasm

indicators.note: go is placed around the other letters, as something about them surrounds them
in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
the start of a word is its opening letter, here of up

explanation.surface: Someone sets off down the road and gets on with things eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go about' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'about' is the container signal wrapping the word go around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty relish or zest in doing something is what this word means.

clue.text: Refuses to carry on with performing singers

indicators.note: performers put on a show, so the letters of singers do a turn and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quits rather than continue alongside a group of vocalists on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steps down from a post declines to continue in it, the sense of quitting.

clue.text: Forwarded about ten cents as a deposit

indicators.note: sent goes around the coin, as a thing about another surrounds it

parts.note: forwarded means sent on
a dime is a US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: Someone sends some small change as a down payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' suggests money, fitting the coins, but here it means matter that settles at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit, a synonym in the geological sense.

clue.text: Certain to remain in step if treated with respect

indicators.note: one word stays inside another, so sure is set within the word for a step

parts.note: a tread is the flat part of a stair you step on
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Advice that one is bound to stay in line if handled with courtesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held dear and cherished is valued highly, which is how it is treated.

clue.text: Spills in outhouses

explanation.surface: Something is knocked over inside the garden huts.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means drops or casts off, as tears or leaves; as a noun, simple garden huts.

clue.text: Survive to the finish on the river

parts.note: an end is a finish
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone lasts until the end of a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out or withstand hardship is a synonym of surviving it.

clue.text: Make notes about a bird taking off hurriedly

indicators.note: sing goes around the bird's name, as one thing about another surrounds it

parts.note: to sing is to make musical notes
a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: Someone jots down observations of a bird as it flies off fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing, but here it means producing musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing off quickly is the informal sense of this verb, as in rushing away.

clue.text: Tyrant was fortunately posted abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters of posted are spread about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictator luckily got sent overseas on assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who wields power cruelly is an autocrat or tyrant.

clue.text: Sculpture which sends you French astray

indicators.note: sends can mean throws into confusion, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: tu is the French word for you
taken as written

explanation.surface: Artwork that makes French visitors lose their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends astray' reads as one phrase, but ASTRAY is fodder alongside TU (French 'you'), and 'sends' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues collectively are sculpture as an art form, a near synonym.

clue.text: Clippings cut from dogs perhaps

parts.note: a snip is a small cut
dogs are an example of pets

explanation.surface: Hair trimmed from the family dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces cut off something are fragments or clippings.

clue.text: Press cutting-or what links some of them together

definitions.text: what links some of them together

explanation.surface: A newspaper clipping and the fastener that holds several of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press cutting' read as two words gives a paper (press) clip (cutting); the second half is the literal wire fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, a newspaper extract is a clip from the paper; literally, the bent wire holding sheets together.

clue.text: Get artist to stir graduate up in a Sikh centre

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A painter is urged to get a scholar moving in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run RA STIR MA backwards, the down-clue reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Punjab city houses the Golden Temple, the holiest shrine of Sikhism.

clue.text: Help sent back to group leader with the animals took the form of charts

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of group

parts.note: rams are male sheep, animals

explanation.surface: Assistance returns to a herd's leader, and the flock takes shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses AID to give DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts are drawings or plans showing how something works, another word for schematic drawings.

clue.text: Doesn't take responsibility for broadcast with noises all around

indicators.note: the din word goes all around the other, surrounding it

parts.note: dins are loud noises
to sow is to scatter seed broadcast

explanation.surface: A broadcaster disclaims a programme surrounded by racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but it means scattering seed by hand; 'all around' puts the noises around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who repudiates or refuses to acknowledge something rejects any connection with it.

clue.text: Boy who swallowed cannabis did the right thing!

indicators.note: one word swallows another, taking it inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A lad who took drugs is ironically praised for his choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the phrase is an exclamation of approval, 'exactly right', for someone who got it right.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase means exactly correct or perfectly judged, a fit for praising a good choice.

clue.text: Nothing goes with crosses

explanation.surface: Nothing is said to accompany a set of crosses.
explanation.walkthrough: The game of noughts and crosses (tic-tac-toe) pairs these zeros with crosses on a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeros are figures for nothing, and in the paper-and-pencil game they are played against crosses.

clue.text: One of nervous disposition gets a reminder

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious person receives a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of nervous disposition' reads as a description of temperament; 'disposition' is the anagram signal for I plus NERVOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake brought back from a trip serves as a memento, prompting memory.

clue.text: French and Latin, this is the principle

parts.note: et is the French word for and
hic is the Latin word for this

explanation.surface: Combining two old languages yields a guiding rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral rule or set of values guiding behaviour is a principle.

clue.text: Alloy of copper and zinc-or molybdenum and lutetium maybe

parts.note: taken as written
Mo is the chemical symbol for molybdenum
Lu is the chemical symbol for lutetium

explanation.surface: A chemistry note offers alternative metals for a brass-like alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilded bronze or brass with a golden look, used on furniture, is this material.

clue.text: All round vegetable?

parts.note: a bulb that is spherical and made of layer upon layer wrapped all round it

explanation.surface: A question about a vegetable's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: This bulb is a round vegetable built of concentric layers going all the way round.

clue.text: Pure water

explanation.surface: A note about clean water.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means nothing more than, sheer; as a noun, a small lake or pond.

clue.text: Throw out something of value

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or askew, so the letters of throw are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Discarding an item that turns out to be valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw out' reads as discard, but 'out' signals an anagram of THROW.
explanation.definitionFit: The value or merit of something is how much it is deemed good for.

clue.text: Perhaps she will get cod-or even oysters!

parts.note: she'll is the contraction of she will
cod is one kind of fish, and Perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Perhaps a woman will be served cod, or maybe oysters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' at the start marks cod as an example of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters are an example of molluscs and crustaceans eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Agrees to write some letters

explanation.surface: Someone concurs and then writes several letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It means matches or tallies, and also exchanges letters with someone by post.
